author: Bluegrass Times
title: Archdiocese of Louisville to offer Communion Minister Formation sessions in coming months
text:
The Archdiocese of Louisville’s Office of Worship announced on May 6 that it will offer Communion Minister Formation for individuals preparing to serve as extraordinary ministers of Holy Communion, as well as for those currently serving who need to renew their mandate.
This program is structured as a one-session formation and is available on several dates in the coming months. Registration is required at least a week in advance. Interested participants can register online by visiting archlou.org/worship or by emailing worship@archlou.org.
The initiative reflects the Archdiocese’s ongoing efforts to support Catholic spiritual development and community outreach through its ministries, according to the official website . The Archdiocese also maintains archives for historical research, aligns with the Roman Catholic Church as an ecclesiastical territory, aims to spread the Gospel and foster spiritual growth, operates under the guidance of the Archbishop and consultative groups, and provides pastoral care across central Kentucky parishes—all according to its official website .
These formation sessions are intended both for new volunteers seeking preparation and current ministers who require renewal. The process ensures that those distributing Holy Communion are adequately prepared in accordance with church guidelines.
As faith communities continue their activities throughout central Kentucky, these programs aim to reinforce communal worship practices while upholding standards set by church leadership.
